text:
Predicates:
GiveOutRoses(x, y, z) ::: roses are given out on x at y on z.
OnBachelor(x) ::: x is on the Bachelor.
PortrayRealLives(x) ::: x portrays the lives of real people.
RealityTV(x) ::: x is a reality TV show.
Premises:
∃x (Monday(x) ∧ GiveOutRoses(x, 8pm, TV)) ::: On some Mondays at 8 pm, roses are given out on TV.
∀x (GiveOutRoses(x, y, TV) → OnBachelor(x)) ::: Every rose given out on TV is on the Bachelor.
∀x (OnBachelor(x) → PortrayRealLives(x)) ::: Everything on the Bachelor portrays the lives of real people.
∀x (PortrayRealLives(x) → RealityTV(x)) ::: All shows portraying the lives of real people are reality TV shows.
¬RealityTV(BreakingBad) ::: Breaking Bad is not a reality TV show.
Conclusion:
¬(GiveOutRoses(Monday, 8pm, BreakingBad)) ::: Breaking Bad is a TV show in which roses are given out on Monday at 8 pm.
